label:
Żentyca
(zhentytsia)
note: The Ukrainian word zhentytsa also simply means whey, so the same word names the drink and the liquid it is made from.

about.text: A sour drink of the Polish and Ukrainian Carpathians made from sheep's whey left over from making bundz cheese in the shepherds' huts. The whey is heated, the protein that rises is skimmed off, and the rest is left to ferment in a wooden barrel with its own microflora.

links.name: Nutritional value of żentyca, J. Elem.

how.text: Heating the whey to 90 °C makes its proteins coagulate and rise as a thin skin, which is skimmed off and set aside as a cheese-like curd (urda); the whey left behind is poured into a wooden barrel, where the natural microflora of whey and barrel sour it over several days. This account is second-hand, from a summary of the żentyca papers.
